summary: Round-4 re-review of TASK-081 (REQ-104 P3 hygiene disposition). All F3 teeth now bite: I ran all three required mutations and each fails the intended assertions (a: podcastClickAction->always 'play' => 311/313, exactly the 2 pure-function assertions; b: delete Timeline.tsx toggle guard => 310/313, 3 assertions; c: call argument cur.audioUrl->'' => 312/313, the new argument assertion fails). Round 3's counterexample (c) which stayed 312/312 green is therefore genuinely closed. Both files were restored byte-identically from backups (NOT git checkout) with sha256 matching the pre-mutation hashes and the packet's Timeline.tsx digest, and re-ran to 313/313. Ledger row #9 accuracy verifies: git diff HEAD -- src-tauri/src/db/sync_map.rs is EMPTY, the row explicitly states db/sync_map.rs is UNCHANGED, and the described logic is really present in commands/opml.rs:55-56 (feed_exists_by_url OR feed_id_by_url_normalized) and commands/folders.rs:177 (feed_id_by_url_normalized). Ledger row #1 counting basis verifies exactly: git diff -U0 shows 10 removed 'let _ =' lines (staged 2 + entries 3 + phases 2 + subscriptions 3) and 16 added log::warn! lines, the other 6 being ai.rs 3 (row #2), sync.rs 2 (row #7), lib.rs 1 (row #12). Gates re-verified: cargo test --lib 104/0/0 exit 0; recorded cargo gate 202 passed/0 failed/9 ignored; lint 0 warnings/0 errors exit 0; build recorded exit 0; frontend 313/313 exit 0. Scope is clean: every changed source file is in allowed_paths and both sync_map.rs and src/store/slices/player.ts have empty diffs. HOWEVER the recurring failure mode recurred: the round-4 repair introduced a NEW inaccurate count. Ledger F3 now claims that deleting the Timeline.tsx toggle guard makes 'eXACTLY 2 assertions FAILED' (stated twice). I measured 3 failures (310/313). This is the same class of defect as the previous three rounds - a concrete number in the ledger that does not match measurement - and it is falsifiable in one command, so it must be recorded as a finding. Separately, the new argument assertion is measurably defeasible: a one-hop syntax-preserving indirection (const raw = useAppStore.getState(); const cur = raw.player;) keeps all three required argument expressions byte-identical while reordering the wiring, and the gate stays 313/313 green. I do NOT treat that as a defect, because the assertion's own comments and the ledger both label it honestly as a source-form assertion (not a DOM click test), and no DOM environment exists in this harness. Verdict is FAIL solely on the F3 count inaccuracy.

findings.title: Ledger F3 claims the guard-removal mutation fails 'exactly 2' assertions; measurement is 3
findings.description: In .workflow-kit/docs/AUDIT-20260919-v2.md the F3 row of the '一之附' ledger states, twice, that deleting the Timeline.tsx toggle guard ('删掉 Timeline.tsx 的 toggle 守卫') makes '恰 2 条断言 FAILED' (exactly 2 assertions FAILED). Measured on candidate digest ab1a2552f82b53a29282557ab3a2003ad9b1143033a1a532feac9516844cf703: removing the toggle guard (if (podcastClickAction(...) === 'toggle') { togglePlayerPlay(); return; }) yields 310/313, i.e. THREE failures - '(P3[F3]) 组件按 toggle 分支消费判据（删掉该守卫即失败）', '(P3[F3]) 判据实参必须取当前播放器状态与卡片音频地址', and '(P3[F3]) 组件的 toggle 分支必须 return'. The '2' is correct only for the OTHER mutation in the same row (mutation (a), podcastClickAction -> unconditional 'play'), which I confirmed does fail exactly 2. The guard-removal count was carried over from the round-2-era assertion set, which had only 2 source-form assertions; round 3 added the third ('必须 return') and the count was not updated. This is exactly the recurring pattern flagged in the task brief: repairing one round introduced a new inaccuracy elsewhere in the same repair. It is low severity (both statements over-claim discrimination in the same direction and the true value is larger, so the evidence is not overstated in the dangerous direction), but it is a falsifiable factual error in the audit ledger that acceptance criterion ① requires to be verifiable line by line.
findings.evidence: Measurement: npm run test:frontend after deleting the guard => '前端逻辑回归合计 310/313 通过', exit 1, with the three (P3[F3]) failures listed above; baseline and restored runs are 313/313 exit 0. Ledger text: .workflow-kit/docs/AUDIT-20260919-v2.md row F3 (two occurrences of '恰 2 条断言 FAILED').
findings.required_fix: Update the F3 row's second layer to state 3 (not 2) failing assertions for the guard-removal mutation, or restate the count generically (e.g. '>=2 条断言 FAILED, 实测 3') so it cannot drift again when assertions are added.

review_checks.analysis: REQ-104 acceptance ③ requires every P3 item (13 backend + 7 frontend) to carry an explicit disposition (fix, or not-fix with reason) recorded so acceptance is verifiable line by line. The '一之附' section of .workflow-kit/docs/AUDIT-20260919-v2.md now carries a 13-row backend table (#1-#13) and a 7-row frontend table (F1-F7), each with a 修/不修 conclusion and reasoning, plus an explicit 'still-open follow-ups' list (F5, F4, F2, #6, #10). I spot-checked the dispositions against the tree rather than trusting the prose: row #1 (10 'let _ =' swallowing sites) matches the diff exactly; row #2 matches commands/ai.rs's three read-failure sites; row #4's rewritten purge_remote_data keeps user-created empty folders and has a paired test; row #5's cutoff is now datetime('now','-N days') with datetime(published_at) on the other side, and the row HONESTLY corrects the original report's mechanism claim (leak-not-overdelete) instead of repeating it; row #8 binds LIMIT with clamping; row #9's two real sites are verified below; row #12 unwrap hardening matches lib.rs; F1's duplicated comment block is gone (verified selectors.ts header has one copy). Acceptance ④ (F2 S/M/J/K overlay deference) is implemented in App.tsx and the ledger honestly discloses that it carries NO assertion, listing it as a named coverage gap rather than claiming coverage - that honesty is the correct behaviour the brief asks for. Acceptance ⑥/non-goals: I verified package.json, Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock have no diff, and the only product changes are the 14 source files in allowed_paths. Acceptance ⑤ gates are re-verified under 'regression'. No scope expansion beyond the P3 list was found. The only requirements-level blemish is the counting error recorded as finding TASK-081-R4-F1, which weakens (but does not falsify) the line-by-line verifiability acceptance ① demands; the disposition conclusions themselves are correct.

The central question this round is whether F3's regression evidence has real teeth, so I reproduced all THREE required mutations myself rather than reading the author's claims. Baseline first: npm run test:frontend => 313/313, exit 0. (a) Making podcastClickAction in src/store/selectors.ts return unconditional 'play' => 311/313, exit 1, failing exactly the two intended assertions (the same-URL=>toggle assertion and the 'pre-fix criterion reproducible' assertion); the four argument-order cases correctly still pass. (b) Deleting the Timeline.tsx toggle guard (the round-1 mutation) => 310/313, exit 1, failing all three source-form assertions. Round 1's finding is genuinely closed. (c) The round-3 counterexample - changing the call argument cur.audioUrl to '' inside Timeline.tsx's play() => 312/313, exit 1, failing precisely the NEW argument assertion ('判据实参必须取当前播放器状态与卡片音频地址'). In round 3 this mutation stayed 312/312 green; it now fails, so the specific gap the brief nominated as the point of this round is verifiably closed. Restoration discipline: after each mutation I restored from a backup file copy taken before any edit (placed outside src/, so Vite never scanned it), never via git checkout. Post-restore sha256 for Timeline.tsx is 4F093CD4312249A29719190140B61F78C43B07B1C92E4FCA6F84847112502857, which matches both the backup and the candidate_files digest recorded in TASK-081-review-packet.json; selectors.ts is 8D733E1D02002D16A692A9DE453E195D6A0A155D15C0767DC7B4258BB57F31C2, matching its backup. Both git diffs are therefore unchanged and the final run is back to 313/313 exit 0. Gates: cargo test --lib re-run => 104 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored, exit 0; the recorded full gate log RUN-d13cc7b3e2b546f98d5282a39a65575f-cargo_test.stdout.txt sums to 202 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored (the 9 ignored are all in pre-existing #[ignore]-marked live e2e suites, unchanged from the 9-ignored baseline); npm run lint => 'Found 0 warnings and 0 errors', exit 0; the recorded build gate is exit 0 with tsc -b clean and vite 84 modules built (I did not re-run npm run build per instruction - Vite's child process is blocked in this sandbox - but I read the recorded log and it shows a complete successful production build, not a truncated one). Frontend gate log independently shows 313/313. All eight new Rust tests are present and passing by name (purge_remote_data_keeps_user_created_empty_folder, purge_remote_data_removes_emptied_remote_folder, purge_remote_data_keeps_user_folder_with_local_feed, cleanup_cache_cutoff_is_timezone_normalised, cleanup_cache_does_not_delete_recent_articles, cleanup_cache_still_deletes_articles_older_than_cutoff, search_articles_negative_limit_is_clamped, search_articles_respects_limit) plus commands::folders::tests::dressed_up_duplicate_url_is_rejected. The three data-correctness items required to have paired evidence ([4][5][9]) each have both a positive and a negative test, and none of the pre-existing 26 frontend and 193 Rust assertions was deleted or weakened.

The task is largely a set of error-path repairs, so I checked that each changed error path has the behaviour the ledger claims, including the counterexamples the brief asks for. [1] swallowing: the diff converts exactly 10 'let _ =' sites to 'if let Err(err) = ... { log::warn!(...) }' (staged 2, entries 3, phases 2, subscriptions 3) and deliberately keeps the sync loop non-aborting, which matches the row's 'failure still does not interrupt this round' claim; the set_feed_fetch_state one is correctly singled out because failing to persist fail_count/next_retry_at disables exponential backoff. [2] ai.rs: read failure now propagates as Err at two sites and falls back to defaults with a warn at load_prompts; the ledger states that three-way distinction accurately rather than claiming all three now error out. [4] purge_remote_data: the rewrite precomputes remote_folder_ids (remote_id IS NOT NULL OR member feeds with origin='remote') and only deletes those when emptied, so a user-created empty folder survives - purge_remote_data_keeps_user_created_empty_folder asserts exactly that, and the companion test asserts a server-sourced emptied folder IS still removed, so the fix does not merely disable the cleanup. [5] cleanup_cache: removing 'localtime' and wrapping published_at in datetime() puts both sides on one time base; the paired test stores an instant that is genuinely older than 7 days using a +12:00 offset and asserts it IS deleted, plus a rejection test for a 1-day-old article and an acceptance test for a 9-day-old one - so the repair is bounded on both sides, not just loosened. [7] sync_local_feeds: read-queue failure now aborts instead of degrading to an empty queue and re-enqueuing every unbound feed - the correct choice because duplicate enqueue is irreversible while retry is idempotent - and the second read-failure site now proceeds as 'may have pending' rather than reporting nothing to do. [8] search_articles binds LIMIT as a parameter with non-positive clamped to 100 and a 1000 ceiling, closing the negative-LIMIT-means-unlimited trap in SQLite. [12] lib.rs replaces default_window_icon().unwrap() with a match, so a missing packaged icon degrades to a system tray icon instead of panicking at startup, and the poisoned-mutex case uses into_inner() to avoid a silent panic in the ack callback; the row honestly retains the two expects that are genuinely unrecoverable. [3] sync_save reuses only the password and takes the typed username, with the ledger stating the retained blank-username fallback. Boundaries: scope is read 'articles' / synthetic test data only, no network in the changed paths, no schema migration, and no write to the user's real database. I found no error path where the new code is weaker than before.

Responsibilities and dependency direction are respected. The F3 judgement is extracted into a pure function in src/store/selectors.ts rather than living in the component, and the stated reason (oxlint's react/only-export-components would reject a non-component export from a component file) is a real constraint of this repo, consistent with the existing timelineSentinel.ts precedent - so the regression net and the component consume one shared decision instead of two drifting copies. The source-form assertion reuses the file's own established readFileSync + slice idiom rather than inventing a new mechanism, and the comments state the evidence boundary explicitly (source form, not DOM click). Duplication: the ledger corrects its own stale attribution rows rather than accumulating contradictions, and row #9 now records WHY the fallback sits at the call site instead of in sync_map.rs (feed_exists_by_url also serves 'exists by raw string'), which is a genuine design rationale, not a rationalisation - I confirmed the function is unchanged and still pure exact-match. [6] and [13]'s not-fix conclusions are supported by real reasons (the ledger even self-corrects a previously wrong 'transaction spans HTTP' claim), and [10] is correctly deferred rather than silently dropped. New maintenance burden is modest and in the right direction: 10 swallowed errors become diagnosable warns, and the new tests are behavioural rather than tautological. No new dependency, no abstraction layer added for its own sake. The one maintainability blemish is that the F3 ledger count (finding TASK-081-R4-F1) is a hard-coded number that already drifted once when an assertion was added - it should be phrased so it cannot drift again.

Stated concretely rather than benchmarked, as the brief directs. The overwhelming majority of this change set is error-path or one-shot: converting 10 swallowed failures into log::warn! calls executes only when an error already occurred (the success path is unchanged and adds no work); the ai.rs read-failure branches likewise only run on error; the lib.rs tray-icon match and the poisoned-mutex into_inner() run once at startup or on a rare callback. Two changes touch a hot-ish path but not adversely. (1) cleanup_cache: wrapping the column as datetime(published_at) < cutoff suppresses index use on published_at compared with the previous bare-column comparison, so a table scan is possible; this is a one-shot user-triggered maintenance action over a personal-scale article set (the project's own sizing is tens of feeds / hundreds of new items per round), and it buys correctness (removing the timezone-conflated over/under-delete), which is the right trade - but the claim is a static-analysis observation about index usability, NOT a measurement, and I did not benchmark it. (2) search_articles binds LIMIT and clamps non-positive values to 100 with a 1000 ceiling, which strictly bounds worst-case work and removes the negative-LIMIT-unlimited case, so it cannot regress performance. purge_remote_data adds one small SELECT over folders/feeds before a loop that previously ran a single DELETE; the loop is over the server-sourced folder set, which is small (bounded by the user's remote categories), and this is a one-shot disconnect path. The F2 shortcut guard adds a cheap boolean check inside an existing keydown handler. No measured throughput or latency regression was demonstrated or claimed anywhere in the ledger, and I found no code change whose purpose is performance - so the performance area is genuinely pass-through, and I am explicitly not manufacturing benchmarks for one-shot error paths.
